I found 14 of the 92 households outside their IPS on 15 April 2026, and none of them has a documented exception. Four have a single stock above the concentration limit, one has both a stock above the limit and asset classes out of band, and nine have asset classes out of band only. This memo sets out what the records show; it draws no legal conclusion.

**How I checked.** For each household I added up the custodian's 15 April 2026 positions and cash, grouped the holdings using the asset-class map in that household's IPS, and compared each stock and each asset class with the household's limit and bands. The portfolio system's positions match the custodian's (same 688 positions; I checked the values line by line for six of the candidates). I searched every household's CRM and found no exception, waiver or client-signed acknowledgment of any kind. The most recent annual review notes (2025-10-14) say only "No changes requested."

**A stock above the concentration limit**
- **HH-0376:** Fenwright Networks Group (SEC-0032) is 37.7% of the household; the limit is 30%.
- **HH-0816:** Halvern Health Holdings (SEC-0005) is 49.1%; the limit is 20%.
- **HH-0221:** Varrick Pharma Holdings (SEC-0040) is 40.3%; the limit is 25%.
- **HH-0984:** Ardley Rail Group (SEC-0048) is 35.8%; the limit is 30%.
- **HH-3058:** Bramwell Devices Group (SEC-0028) is 32.5%; the limit is 15%.

In all five the stock built up from quarterly employer share grants (restricted stock units) delivered into one account. Each household sold only one grant's worth or none (HH-3058 sold two, in December 2025).

**Asset classes outside their bands**

| Household | US equity (target) | Int'l equity (target, band) | Fixed income (target) |
|---|---|---|---|
| HH-3058 | 68.1% (60%) | 4.1% (10% ±4) | 15.0% (28%) |
| HH-3462 | in band | in band | 17.7% (30%) |
| HH-8865 | 70.7% (55%) | – | 28.5% (40%) |
| HH-8312 | 72.1% (55%) | – | 27.0% (40%) |
| HH-9571 | 65.7% (55%) | in band | 24.5% (30%) |
| HH-9234 | 65.3% (55%) | in band | 24.5% (30%) |
| HH-5814 | 55.9% (50%) | in band | 33.0% (40%) |

| HH-6590 | 50.2% (45%) | in band | 40.6% (47%) |

Bands are ±5 points unless shown otherwise. HH-6590 and HH-6047 are only just over the US equity band (by 0.24 and 1.6 points), but they are also below the fixed income band.

**What a reviewer may want to look at**
- In HH-3058 and HH-3462, the proceeds of December 2025 stock sales are still sitting as cash (about $440K and $430K). That cash is a large part of why fixed income is under its band.
- In HH-9571 and HH-9234, the firm bought more Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund (a US equity fund) in November–December 2025, which added to holdings in a class that is now above its band.
- In HH-8865 and HH-8312, a joint owner died in 2025. The joint account still lists both owners and holds most of the excess equity.
- HH-7350's concentration limit carries a 2020 date, unlike every other IPS. It makes no difference: its stocks are well under the limit.
- All other stock holdings are under their limits. That includes HH-0193's Corriden Card Holdings at 18.8% against a 27% limit and HH-0926's Fallowmere Utilities Group at 17.2% against 30%.
